recipes.name: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ingredients_raw: 1 pound andouille or smoked sausage, sliced 1/4 inch thick
1 pinch Creole seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a stockpot over medium heat; whisk in flour until roux is smooth and has cooked to the color of chocolate milk, about 8 to 10 minutes. Be careful not to burn the roux. If you see black specks in the mixture, it's best to start over.
Add sausage, celery, bell pepper, and onion into the roux; cook and stir 5 minutes. Add garlic; continue to cook and stir another 5 minutes.

Season with salt, pepper, and Creole seasoning; stir well to blend. Pour in chicken broth and add bay leaf. Bring to a boil over high heat; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chicken and simmer 1 hour more. Skim off any foam that floats to the top during this time.

raw_recipe.headline: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
raw_recipe.description: This chicken and sausage gumbo uses a roux as the thickening agent in this traditional Cajun-style gumbo that's rich and hearty with lively seasonings.

video.description: This is a Cajun-style gumbo made with a seasoned roux, a classic from the bayous of south Louisiana. Full of flavor and spice, the longer you let it simmer, the tastier the gumbo becomes! Serve it hot over cooked rice or with potato salad.

review.reviewBody:
Hi everyone, I am the author of this recipe and from reading the reviews I thought I would add...the roux color is really dependent on how you would like it. I used milk chocolate as a reference as that's our family preference. If you would like it darker then you would just keep a stirrin until it's a color you would desire-it also intensifies the flavor. Also, if you do not like it thick then reduce the flour/oil ratio to maybe 1/2 c. flour to 1/2 c. oil. Thanks to everyone for trying the gumbo!!

Jodi

This recipe is fantastic! I had been looking for a tomato-free gumbo recipe for a while! A note to anyone who said that it turned out too greasy because of the full cup of oil: it probably needs to cook longer. A lot longer. I recently stumbled upon an easy oven roux recipe that changed my life (my gumbo-making life, that is). Pre-heat the oven to 375 degrees. In a cast iron dutch oven, heat 1 cup of oil. After heated, slowly add a cup of flour and whisk thoroughly and heat through. Then, just transfer the whole dutch oven into the pre-heated oven and cook for 1 1/2 to 2 hours (your preference, I like my roux DARK). All you have to do is take it out every 20 minutes and whisk it a little. BEST roux I've ever made. Ever. And no standing over a hot stove all day! 8-10 minutes on the stove is just not enough, not even close. Everything else in this recipe is spot-on though. If the roux is cooked properly, you won't see any oil or grease floating to the top because it's been fully cooked and incorporated into the flour. Oh! And I added about 1 1/2 cups of frozen okra the last 10 minutes or so. Just a personal preference... I love okra!

Just letting others know that Olive Oil worked great for the roux ( possibly healthier ) I let it color slowly with the flour to a nice dark reddish brown - about 20 mins or more stirring very frequently. Also, I added uncooked chicken tenders in the first hour and then roughly cut and returned to broth before serving. I also added ground hot Italian sausage instead of the Andoulie - added before the 2 hour simmer. I use the Creole seasoning from 'all recipes' and keep it in a jar for next time. I used about 2 tsps and it was fabulous.

This recipe is so good! It was my first time making gumbo, but it sure won’t be the last! 
I made a few very slight changes, based on comments and what I had on hand: used 1/2 c. oil and 3/4 c. flour, used some chicken thighs I had on hand, didn’t have a bay leaf, and I added about 4 c. of sliced okra.
For the creole seasoning, I used a recipe I found on this site (cut the salt in half), and added 3 T. of it to the gumbo. 
Served the gumbo over rice, and our taste buds were happy, happy, happy!

Only saying 4 stars because the roux is too much oil and flour - 1/2 cup oil and flour is plenty. Otherwise? Crystal hot sauce, good rice - perfect meal. Have made this many times. I usually use a combo of thighs and wings to get a good broth and soft meat. Dark roux makes it exceptional. No tomatoes!

Fabulous recipe! I did follow a suggestion from another and made my roux in the oven - it was fabulous! Used 2/3 cup of vegetable oil and 1 cup of flour. Mix on the stove with whisk - oven on 375 - then place in the oven. I did so for two hours stirring every 20 minutes. It was perfect. As with other reviewers, I swapped green pepper for cut okra (frozen 14 ounce) the last 30 minutes. I did have to add some additional broth and one cup of water for my desired consistency as it simmered. It was a big hit!

This is as good as I've ever had. My family and I enjoyed every bite! It takes a lot of attention even after the roux is ready. Lots of stirring and scraping the bottom of the pot. I recommend using a metal spatula and enamel or cast iron cookware. I used boneless chicken breast instead of rotisserie, chopping and searing it prior to starting the gumbo recipe. This will definitely be a new favorite around here!

Pretty Awesome! Just finished eating 2 bowls and the family loved it! Read most of the ratings and tried a few ideas with success. Plus being from N.O. I knew right off the bat what extras I needed. Fried the sausage prior, added 1 tbs of seasoning, 1/4 tsp red pepper, 1/4 tsp thyme, 30min before done added okra, 5min before done added shrimp. Instructions were dead-on and easy to follow. You rock YOYO78! Thanks for sharing.

Absolutely the best thing I have ever made from AllRecipes!! Sooo flavorful! Followed the recipe almost precisely, but made slight changes. A few things come out a bit different than expected. The onion, celery, and green pepper are delicious, but completely cook away. Needs the presence of some veggies. Add 1lb fresh cut frozen okra toward the end, about 10 minutes before eating, makes the gumbo perfect. Also doubled the celery at the beginning. Thickened it with 2 tablespoons of flour later in cooking, liquid now thicker, like stew. Used 3lbs of chicken breast, not rotissiere. Used a big teaspoon of salt, pepper, & Zataran's creole seasoning. Delicious and inexpensive. Making again today. Really good on rice, even better on cheese grits. YUM!!!

This is wonderful... My family loved it. I cut the oil in half for the roux...used Tony's for the seasoning. Simmered cubed chicken breast in a little water in a frying pan then threw it in the gumbo about 45 min before it was done. Use long grain rice cooked in chicken broth. I quadrupled this recipe in a stock pot. It's even better the next day.

Next time I will definitely use only half the fat and flour; the broth was much too thick for my taste. I used butter instead of vegetable oil. Also, it seemed like it needed more vegetables, so I chopped three carrots and added them. Okra would have been good, too, if I had it on hand. The sausage was so spicy (Aidell's brand), that a tablespoon of Tony Chachere's was plenty!
Follow this recipe and you will be thrilled with the results. The only thing I do is I also add shrimp at the end. This is now a family favorite.

I AM MARRIED TO A CAJUN RAISED MAN. I WAS EXCITED ABOUT THIS RECIPE. THE FAMILY ENJOYED IT, BUT HE HAD TO ADD A LOT MORE OF A VERY POPULAR LOUISIANA CHEF TO BRING THE FLAVOR UP. I ONLY HAD WESSON OIL AND AVOCADO OIL SO I OPTED FOR WESSON. I BELIEVE THAT THE OIL WOULD HAVE MADE A DIFFERENCE. WHAT BRAND OR KINDS OF OIL WOULD YOU RECOMMEND? TO MY TASTE, I FELT LIKE THE ROUX WAS THIN LIKE TURKEY GRAVY. SINCE MY ENTIRE FAMILY LIKED IT, I WILL GIVE THIS A 5. WOULD BUTTER AND FLOUR MAKE A GOOD ROUX? I AM A NOVICE, I DO NOT KNOW. I LOVE ALLRECIPES, AS IT MAKES COOKING EASY AND UNDERSTANDABLE!

Definitely keeping this in my favorite list. I added a teaspoon of Cayenne pepper, since our family likes it on the spicy side. Other then that, its a very flavorful dish. Thank you for putting it out there.
I didn’t feel comfortable enough with getting to the chocolate milk stage, but it cooked long enough. Great recipe and results.
Was good!
I did let the roux cook longer and added shredded carrots.

Everytime I make Gumbo THIS is the recipe I go with! As someone who is from Louisiana I can tell you every Momma making gumbo at home uses the most simple ingredients, this is the only recipe I've ever found that is truly spot on to how people ACTUALLY cook gumbo In southern LA.

Made this recipe for the second time. I substituted butter for the oli. It was exactly as I hoped it would turn out. We had leftovers, so I added some baby spinach to the gumbo, filled tortillas and topped with some salsa verde and baked 15 minutes. Delicious gumbo enchiladas!
Awesome!!!!
